hypothesis: Keeping the baseline cut/balance/binarisation backbone untouched, adding a case-relative criticality-weighted net-cut multiplier (1 + alpha * mean-pin criticality rank) steers only the few most timing-critical nets to stay within a tier, reducing crit-pair cross-tier and hence TNS, while alpha is kept small so non-critical nets are not sacrificed.
analysis: Hypothesis failed: crit_cross rose in all circuits (C1 0.011→0.104, C2 0.000→0.097, C3 0.069→0.112) despite lower cut/wcut and fewer repair flips—criticality weighting apparently perturbed the backbone away from timing-critical containment, worsening dWNS (−9 to −27%) and dTNS. Seed spread is unacceptable (std 0.349; per-seed signs flip, e.g. C3 +0.45/−0.63). Next: verify the criticality rank is correctly aligned with crit-pair membership and sweep alpha downward (or gate the multiplier only on nets already near-tier-boundary) before retraining.
